Archive Access for Non-Commercial Use BBC Archives manages one of the world's largest multimedia archives - find out ways you can access and research BBC Archive content. BBC Archive Curated extracts from the BBC's huge content archive. Visit the BBC Archive website BBC Programme Listings To find listings information, people, dates or times of a particular programme, BBC Programme Listings is a searchable database of the BBC's broadcasts from 1923-2009 derived from the Radio Times magazine listings. BBC Television Archive The British Film Institute (BFI) provides public, on-request access to the BBC Television Archive. It provides research and viewing services but does not supply copies of BBC Television content. BBC Radio Archive The British Library Sound Archive provides public on-request access to, and listening facilities for, a collection of BBC radio recordings. It cannot supply copies of BBC material. BBC Written Archives The BBC Written Archives Centre contains thousands of files, scripts and working papers from all parts of the BBC, since the BBC's formation in 1922. BBC Photo Library A commercial, fee paying service which licenses BBC copyright images for editorial use in digital and print media. This service is not available to members of the public for private use. BBC Contributor Access Service People who have made a substantial contribution to a BBC programme, either as a featured or named contributor, may be able to purchase a copy for personal use. BBC Sound Effects Some of the BBC SFX collection is now available for personal, educational or research purposes. For commercial use you can access and license the whole collection through a third party. Educational access The entire digitised BBC broadcast archive is now available to teachers, schools and students in formal education in the UK. BBC Teach has information on how it can be accessed. BBC Studios Learning BBC Studios Learning license full-length programmes for educational purposes. A number of providers offer access to BBC broadcasts for UK HE and FE institutions in possession of an ERA licence, including BoB National, Planet eStream and ClickView. Commercial Use BBC Studios Distribution sells radio and TV clips via the BBC Motion Gallery library sales service, in partnership with Getty Images. Non-Commercial Use How to use BBC content, including whole programmes, clips, photos and content from bbc.co.uk. During the session, he also spoke about his love of jazz and his work with the Community Music Workshop. Having recently performed at Ronnie Scott's, Pine expressed his hope that more Black musicians would join the jazz scene Clip taken from Ebony, originally broadcast on BBC Two, 13 December 1985 . BBC Archive:  Britain declares war on Germany in 1939 - BBC BBC Homepage Skip to content Accessibility Help Your account Home News Sport Earth Reel Worklife Travel Culture Future Music TV Weather Sounds More menu More menu Search BBC Home News Sport Earth Reel Worklife Travel Culture Future Music TV Weather Sounds Close menu 1939: Britain declares war on Germany 1939: Britain declares war on Germany Close At 11.15am, the news that the country is at war is communicated to the population of the United Kingdom. Chamberlain's famous words are followed by government announcements warning that air raids are expected to follow quickly. In the preceding months, Chamberlain and the government had planned to shut down BBC broadcasts in the event of hostilities, believing they were unnecessary during wartime. However, their value in providing information and boosting morale soon became obvious. Note: there is a gap in this recording between Chamberlain's announcement and the follow up announcement read by Alvar Lidell. Originally broadcast on the Home Service on 3 September 1939.
